lead: A local declared inside a loop body stays declared for the rest of the enclosing scope, so a second loop cannot reuse the name.
body: `bytes $sealed` inside one `while` and `bytes $sealed` inside the next is `E0406: $sealed is already declared`, which reads as a scoping bug rather than as the rule. Give the second pass its own name (`$stored`, `$openedKey`) when a program walks the same shape twice, which every "seal it, then read it back" example does.
